blocks.text: Ever since the introduction of the telephone, there have been new problems arising from the carrying of signals or messages. At the beginning, each signal was carried by means of a pair of overhead wires; soon after, telephone exchanges were surrounded by thousands of wires. The cables replaced the wires. Each of them contained many pairs of wires and therefore they were capable of carrying many signals. These cables were laid underground and they replaced the overhead wires.

The more extensive telephone services have become, the more the demand for these services has increased, particularly the demand for long distance services. Long-distance telephone exchanges are usually located in crowded cities, where it is costly and inconvenient to lay new cables for expanding services.

blocks.text: Study the following dialogues. Practice them with a partner.

items: *1.– A)* Do you have a phone, Mr. Jones?
*B)* No, but my cousin has one. His number is 699-7701.
*2.– A)* I’d like the number of the Perkins living on Third Street.. (To the operator)
*B)* There are many Perkins living on that Street. Do you have a first name?
*B)* It’s impossible to find it without a first name.
*4.– A)* Long distance? I’d like to make a person-to-person call to Dan Osmond in Texas.
*B)* You’ll have to call information. The area code is 996.
*5.– A)* Hello, this is Alice. May I speak to Liz?
*A)* Would you please tell her I’ll call again?
*6.– A)* I’d like to speak to Mr. Frank Brown. Is he there?
*B)* I’m afraid you have the wrong number. What number were you calling?
*B)* This is Beverly Hills, 7-2821. But there is no one by the name of Brown here.
*A)* I must have made a mistake. I’m sorry to have bothered you.
*B)* Hello. This is a collect call, operator.

blocks.title: Function: Instructions. Clarifying information on the phone.

groups.after: do if the line is not engaged?

groups.label: 3.– Is there anything special I should

items: First check the code (if any) and number.
Lift the receiver and listen for dialing tone (a continuous purring).
Dial carefully and allow the dial to return freely.
Ringing tone (burr-burr) the number is being called.
Engaged tone (a repeated single note) try again a few minutes later.
Number unobtainable tone (steady note) replace reciever, re-check the code and number, and then re-dial.
After dialing a trunk call there will be a pause before you hear a tone; during this time the trunk equipment will be connecting your call.
At the end of the call, replace the reciever securely because timing of calls stops when the caller hangs up.
Always give your name or telephone number.
If you hear a series of rapid pips, the call is coming from a coinbox telephone. Wait until the pips stop and then give your name or telephone number.

blocks.text: III. Clarifying information on the phone

items: Could you spell that for me, please?
I can’t follow you. Could you speak a little slower?
Could you speak up a little?
Would you mind speaking a bit more slowly?
Sorry, I can’t hear you very well.
Would you mind saying that again?
Would you like to leave a message?
Excuse me. What was that again?
You have my word on it.
